debates.topic: How much shorter do new programs get in S2 (capability-program-cycle-compression)
debates.skeptic_view: The 38% is an Amdahl ceiling, not the expected result. Requirements negotiation, hardware-in-the-loop testing and review gates do not compress 5-10x, and long-lead parts run in parallel with design. Realized compression is 15-25% in S2, first visible in 2031.
debates.advocate_view: The bound wrongly treats integration and test, procurement and reviews as wholly physical. Splitting out the analysis inside them gives 45-50% in S2 and 59-64% in S3. Uncrewed commercial programs need no certifier, so the Medium cap and the qualification gate are misapplied. S2 2029, S3 High.
debates.resolution: The 38% is presented as a ceiling, and the realized S2 range is set at 20-30%, between the two views. The advocate's split mostly double-counts: the table's 1.1-1.2x physical multipliers already credit about 10 of the 60 'physical' points as compressing cognitive work. Accepted from the advocate: the binding gate becomes experiment, and design optimization becomes an accelerator. Accepted from the skeptic: S2 2031 and S3 2030, because only programs started after the 2028 adoption count. The advocate's S2 2029 and S3 High are rejected.

debates.topic: When space engineering routinely adopts on-demand math (capability-engineering-adoption, S2)

debates.advocate_view: Move S2 to 2027. SpaceX owns a frontier lab and needs neither public release nor ITAR accreditation. NASA's 22% staff loss pulls toward AI substitution.
debates.resolution: S2 stays 2028 and S3 moves to 2028. The node requires routine use of checked answers in design reviews. That needs the Oct-2026 capability level in outside hands (mid-to-late 2027 in S2) plus trust tooling (2028), and the S2 premise starts the 5-10x cognitive multiplier in 2028. The first-mover point is kept as text in the why field. Because of this, the advocate's dependent proposals (AI-native spacecraft in 2028, program compression in 2029) are also rejected.

debates.advocate_view: S2 2028 -> 2027, and make infra-verified-numerics soft because interval tools (Arb, INTLAB, VNODE-LP) already exist. 2027 has forcing events: GSO operators may try to bring back aggregate limits through reconsideration, the D.C. Circuit or the WRC-27 cycle. The leading filer owns a frontier lab, and Part 100 self-certification needs no regulator to accept the method.
debates.resolution: Soft edge accepted, since the interval-arithmetic tools exist. S2 stays 2028 and S3 becomes 2028. The primary source shows FCC 26-26 puts private coordination first and declined aggregate limits, which weakens the 2027 forcing event. Public applied math arrives in 2027 and a filing takes months to prepare. Bands stay High.

debates.topic: D2D coexistence scheduling timing and band
debates.skeptic_view: Make network-optimization a soft edge. Bands Low/Medium/Medium, S1 2031, S3 2029. The node is dated the same year as its bounds, the harmonics problem is set by filters, and the incentive to protect science bands is weak.
debates.advocate_view: S2 2029 -> 2028, bands unchanged (High). This is a software change on satellites the operator already flies. One vertically integrated actor owns the D2C satellites, the AWS-4/H-block spectrum and a frontier lab. SkyShare already works on Starlink geometry, and WRC-27 agenda item 1.13 sharpens the incentive.
debates.resolution: Soft edge, S1 2031 Low and S2 Medium accepted; the auditor also pushed S2 down. S3 stays High and 2028 as the optimistic, vertically integrated path, now that 'achieved' no longer needs an FCC order and so carries no regulator cap. The advocate's S2 2028 is rejected because it assumed bounds in 2027. Agenda item 1.13 added to status and signpost.

debates.topic: Constellation design optimizer bands
debates.skeptic_view: S3 High -> Medium. 'Proven compliance' is an FCC or ITU determination, so the regulator cap applies, and filers must use prescribed methods (ITU-R S.1503).
debates.advocate_view: S2 Medium -> High. All three prerequisites are High by 2028, Part 100 makes compliance data machine-readable, demand is extreme (50,000+ planned satellites, the 1M orbital-data-center filing), and the bar includes a tool vendor shipping a product.
debates.resolution: Neither change. 'Achieved' is now defined as use in a filing's technical annex without regulator acceptance, so no cap applies and S3 stays High. S2 stays Medium: three High prerequisites in conjunction, a P6 default of Low and strong in-house incumbent tools do not support more than 70%.

debates.topic: Crypto-agile architecture and the PQ flight demo: is AI's share thin or the cap misapplied?
debates.skeptic_view: Cryptanalysis is motive, so make it a soft edge. 'Only hedge' is wrong because AES-256 telecommand is already quantum-safe. Verified ML-KEM for AArch64 already exists, so the AI-dependent part is thin. Demo S3 -> 2029.
debates.advocate_view: The Medium cap is misapplied because the achievement needs no certifier. Commercial PQ satellites fly, CNSA 2.0 applies from Jan 2027, and Tamarin/ProVerif and mlkem-native exist. Raise architecture S2/S3 to High, and the demo to High as well.
debates.resolution: Architecture: the cap was misapplied. With achieved defined as one operator flying or contracting a design with machine-checked rekey and update proofs, S2/S3 go to High, consistent with other uncapped P2 tier-4 nodes in S2. All of the skeptic's structural fixes are kept. Demo: stays Medium. Lifting the inherited cap does not make a specific funded and disclosed mission more likely than not, and none is announced. Demo S3 2029 accepted. The advocate's 'AI-assisted AWS proofs' claim is unsupported and was not used.

debates.topic: PQ fleet migration timing and band
debates.skeptic_view: Later and lower: >2031/2031/2030, Speculative/Low/Medium. 'Most new satellites' implies the roughly 3-year median contract lag. 'Machine-checked update paths' is really the procurement-norm content, which mandates do not drive.
debates.advocate_view: Earlier: S2 2029, S3 2028. By count, new satellites are dominated by proliferated LEO (Starlink, Starshield, SDA), which turns over in 12-24 months and updates over the air. CNSA 2.0 makes new NSS acquisitions post-quantum from Jan 2027.
debates.resolution: Split. The count-weighting argument is accepted for the lag, so S2 2030 and S3 2029 stay. The skeptic is accepted on the band: the machine-checked part needs buyers or the dominant operators to choose it, so S2 drops to Low and S1 to >2031/Speculative. The why was rewritten to remove the 'S3 does not beat S2' contradiction.

debates.topic: Machine-checked crypto procurement norm
debates.skeptic_view: S2 Medium -> Low. It needs two institutional steps in sequence (tool qualification, then a solicitation) at SDA's roughly 2-year solicitation cadence. The signpost should count 'require' only, not evaluation credit.
debates.advocate_view: Make infra-tool-qualification a soft edge, because the trusted base is the proof kernel and not the AI generator. Move to S2 2029 / S3 2028.
debates.resolution: Soft edge accepted on the advocate's trusted-base argument. Earlier years rejected: the flight demo has to come first (S2 2029, S3 2029) and politics compresses 1.0x, so S3 moves to 2030. S2 drops to Low on the skeptic's argument (an institutional step after the demo, with one or two solicitation windows left), and the signpost now counts 'require' only.

debates.topic: Software's share of constellation capacity
debates.skeptic_view: S2 Low, S3 2030. Make design-optimizer and code-design soft edges, since their effects do not reach 2026-2031 capacity. Define the share additively; under log attribution the threshold is about 29%.
debates.advocate_view: Redefine as at least 10% over the same hardware with 2026-era software, and raise S3 to High. Cheap mass moves the binding constraint in dense cells to spectral reuse under the 3%/0.1% test, so certified interference math becomes a capacity input.
debates.resolution: Adopted the fixed-hardware definition, which the auditor also proposed, and the skeptic's S2 Low, S3 2030 and soft edges. The advocate's two-curve mechanism went into the why and the branch hook. S3 High rejected, because attribution to AI and disclosure do not compress under S3.

debates.topic: Verified PQC for space processors
debates.skeptic_view: Part of the result already exists without AI (mlkem-native AArch64). Narrow the node to LEON, RISC-V and FPGA targets plus masking, and move S2/S3 to 2028 because flight adoption is held by qualification.
debates.advocate_view: S1 2027 and High: a verified AArch64 ML-KEM already flies-capable on Zynq-class smallsats, so all that remains is a flight program using it.
debates.resolution: Skeptic's view adopted, with S1 also moved to 2029 to keep S1 behind S2. The advocate's path is real, but it is not attributable to the AI-math channel. The advocate's claim that the proofs were AI-assisted is contradicted by the AWS post and the README.

debates.topic: Whether network optimization needs public research-grade models (hard edge)
debates.skeptic_view: Keep cap-research-math-public as the binding prerequisite; only the ceilings edge should become soft.
debates.advocate_view: Make it soft and move S1 to 2027. GPT-6 Astra and AlphaEvolve are already public, and the main operator owns a frontier lab.
debates.resolution: Kept as a hard edge, and S1 stays 2028. S1 is the plateau scenario, and the node's own why ties it to public research-grade models. The advocate's internal-lab path is the S2/S3 story, which is already dated 2027.

debates.topic: When certified meshes run in production (branch thesis)
debates.skeptic_view: Mesh operations move to S2/S3 2029 at Medium, because a live network of more than 10,000 satellites needs emulation, validation and staged rollout. The thesis should say 2029-30.
debates.advocate_view: 2027-28 at a vertically integrated operator (SpaceXAI), 2029-30 elsewhere.
debates.resolution: The thesis says 2029-30 in the base case (Medium) and names the year-earlier vertically integrated path as the optimistic case. Mesh operations is S2/S3 2029, S2 Medium, S3 High.

debates.topic: Code-design adoption speed
debates.skeptic_view: The gate is adoption and standards cycles bind, so move to 2029/2028/2028. 2026 evidence improves minimum-distance tables, not dB.
debates.advocate_view: Proprietary air interfaces and laser ISLs can adopt by firmware. Add a soft edge into CRQC.
debates.resolution: Years moved per the skeptic. The firmware path went into the text with the caveat that fixed-function decoder ASICs need a hardware cycle. The soft edge to CRQC was rejected: classical link codes are not the qLDPC route, which now lives in comms-ai-crqc-resource-cuts.

debates.topic: CRQC before 2031: S2 band (auditor vs skeptic and advocate)
debates.skeptic_view: Keep Speculative. Vendor roadmaps reach the needed scale around 2033 and expert odds are low; S3 Low sits at its upper edge.
debates.advocate_view: Keep the bands, but revisit S2 Speculative -> Low if logical-qubit milestones land in 2027. Error-correction overhead is the second exponential.
debates.resolution: The auditor's S2 Low was rejected 2-to-1. The fabrication gate is unchanged even though resource estimates fell 10-100x. The advocate's revisit trigger is in the signpost, and the new resource-cuts node carries AI's route into this outcome.

debates.topic: When the credibility rulebook for AI-made analysis arrives (physclock-credibility-evidence-standard)
debates.skeptic_view: The named standards revise every 8-10 years (NASA-STD-7009 in 2008, 2016 and 2024). The next base revision falls around 2030-32, so S2 should be 2030, S3 2029 and S1 >2031. A rule counting AI-checked derivations should not come before the 2030 S2 premise for regulator credit of AI proofs.
debates.advocate_view: FDA wrote a risk-based AI-credibility framework (draft, Jan 2025) without machine-checked numerics, and NASA-STD-7009B is already risk-based. A NASA interim directive needs only checked evidence, available in S2 by 2027. So S2 2028, with verified numerics as a soft input.
debates.resolution: Kept S2 2029, S3 2028 and S1 2031. The skeptic's revision-cycle facts went into the why, but the node is met by the faster handbook or interim-directive route, which the skeptic also names. A rulebook also normally comes before project-level credit, so 2029 does not conflict with 2030 proof credit. Took the advocate's soft edge for verified numerics and the FDA precedent. Rejected S2 2028: FDA's draft is guidance for drug submissions, its device guidance took about five years after ASME V&V 40, and agencies adopt last.

debates.topic: How much shorter qualification gets, and when (physclock-qual-cycle-compressed)
debates.skeptic_view: 30-50% contradicts the branch's own physical-gate table (0.8-0.9x in S2, 0.7-0.8x in S3) and the 1.2x Amdahl figure. Data on programs started in 2028 or later cannot report before about 2031. Retitle to 10-30%, S2 2031 Low, S3 2030.
debates.advocate_view: Fewer tests and faster tests multiply to 0.36-0.64x of test-phase time. Commercial operators can skip qualification units, and the S3 qualification multiplier reaches 1.7x. Keep 30-50%, S2 2029, S3 2028 High, and make the analysis-credit and printed-part edges soft.
debates.resolution: Retitled to 15-30% with a 15% threshold. S2 2031 Low, S3 2030 Medium. The advocate's multiplication applies to test-phase time only and still exceeds the experiment multiplier of 1.1-1.3x. The hard edge to analysis credit stays, because the signpost (GAO and ESA data) measures government programs. The commercial route became a soft accelerator through the new commercial node. Both lenses agreed the printed-part edge should be soft.

debates.topic: Certification by analysis for primary structure (struct-cert-by-analysis)
debates.skeptic_view: The node's examples are already allowed by NASA-STD-5001B, so re-scope to credit beyond those allowances. Follow the slipped rulebook to S2 2031 / S3 2030, S2 Low. Make verified FE solvers soft and add test data as a hard prerequisite.
debates.advocate_view: Verified FE solvers are not required (agreed). With the rulebook in 2028, first credit on derivatives lands in S2 2029 / S3 2028, Medium. Operator self-acceptance belongs on a separate commercial node.
debates.resolution: Re-scoped, after checking the 5001B text. Kept S2 2030 / S3 2029 because the rulebook stays at 2029. S2 band Low, because the re-scoped step is strictly harder than today's allowances and leaves one or two years of window. FE solvers made soft (both lenses). Test-data commons added as a hard edge, because 5001B's no-test criteria rely on similarity and correlation. Operator self-acceptance moved to the new commercial node.

debates.topic: A commercial self-risk track (new node physclock-commercial-analysis-first-qual)
debates.skeptic_view: No new node was proposed. The branch already says commercial operators skip tests where they own the risk, so the gain is mainly on government programs, and the gate is physical and institutional.
debates.advocate_view: Most mass to orbit belongs to operators no qualification authority oversees: Part 450 covers public safety only, and SpaceX's own cargo is about 6x the external market. Add a commercial node at S2 2029, High, plus fleet-statistical qualification and envelope licensing.
debates.resolution: Added the commercial node, re-scoped beyond today's protoflight practice, which the advocate's wording described. S2 Medium rather than High: tests catch workmanship errors, a fleet-wide defect is costly, and the step must be stated publicly to count. S3 High. S3 2029, because S3 equals S2 through 2028. Rejected fleet-statistical qualification: the launch-cost half is independent of AI, the fleet-statistics half is not scarce at the one operator that has such a fleet, and it sat in the same year as its prerequisite. Rejected envelope licensing as a near-duplicate of licensing-in-weeks, since Part 450 already allows one license for multiple launches.

debates.topic: Monthly build-fly-fix loops (physclock-test-loop-monthly)
debates.skeptic_view: It duplicates its own prerequisite (12+ flights in 2027 is a ~30-day mean interval) and contradicts it. The physical table gives 38-53 day intervals in S2. Merge it into flight-test-cadence, or set S3 to 2028 Medium.
debates.advocate_view: It is internally inconsistent in the other direction. Since its prerequisite is High in 2027, six intervals of 30 days or less by 2031 must be High in S2.
debates.resolution: Removed the node, which the skeptic proposed and the auditor offered as an alternative. Both lenses showed it carries no information its prerequisite lacks. The flight-test-cadence owner is asked to add mishap analysis as an accelerator and to review its 2027 High against the physical-gate table.

debates.topic: Structural mass gains (struct-structural-mass-step, struct-flown-lighter-structure)
debates.skeptic_view: An industry-wide 5-15% trend cannot appear in the same year as the first flown article (S2 2031), so the mass step moves to >2031. The gains fall on different parts of dry mass. Analysis-based knockdowns already flew on SLS, so the flown-structure S3 band should drop to Low.
debates.advocate_view: Commercial spacecraft need neither SP-8007 nor a regulator. Remove the standards gate, move the flown structure to S2 2030 Medium, and the mass step to S2/S3 Medium with S3 2030. An AI-native spacecraft at S2 2029 High makes a Low mass step inconsistent.
debates.resolution: Edge changes taken from the advocate and auditor: the flown structure now needs imperfection theory and certified margins, not a standards revision. Years and bands for the flown structure unchanged: the lag ladder puts primary structure at 2031+, and attribution needs a public statement. Mass step S2 >2031 (skeptic). The AI-native spacecraft node is a process outcome whose own strongest case says the performance gains are small, so there is no inconsistency. It and design optimization became soft accelerators.

debates.topic: Launch environments (struct-launch-env-margins)
debates.skeptic_view: Maximum predicted environments are already statistical (P95/50). Empirical data suffice for high-cadence vehicles, forcing uncertainty dominates, and providers lack the incentive to tighten published environments. Make mid-frequency vibroacoustics soft and set S2 Low.
debates.advocate_view: SpaceX is both launch provider and customer for about 73.5% of mass to orbit and has every incentive. Starship flight data calibrate the models. S2 2029, S3 2028.
debates.resolution: S2 Low, years unchanged. The advocate's own example undercuts the AI attribution: with abundant Starship data, empirical envelopes need no predictive models, and SpaceX rarely publishes its environments. The vertically integrated route was added to the description and signpost, and mid-frequency vibroacoustics made soft.

debates.topic: Regulators adopting AI review tools (physclock-regulator-ai-capacity)
debates.skeptic_view: No finding on this node. The skeptic applied the same regulator-behavior cap to range and airspace scheduling.
debates.advocate_view: The Medium cap is misapplied, because this is internal tool use, not acceptance of AI evidence. FDA deployed Elsa agency-wide in June 2025. S2 2027, S2/S3 High.
debates.resolution: Kept Medium and set S3 to 2028, as the auditor proposed (S3 equals S2 through 2028). The node's event includes 2-5x reviewer throughput and published review times, which is regulator behavior under the A3 cap. FDA Elsa was added to the status as evidence that adoption can be fast.

debates.topic: Test design and autonomous test stands (physclock-optimal-test-campaigns, physclock-ai-run-test-stands)
debates.skeptic_view: Design of experiments has been mandated in DoD test and evaluation since 2010 and used at NASA Langley since the late 1990s, and qualification matrices did not shrink. Narrow the node to development tests (10-30%). 20-40% calendar compression from autonomous stands exceeds the 1.1-1.3x experiment multiplier, so stands drop to S2 Medium.
debates.advocate_view: The first adopter, SpaceXAI, does not wait for industry-wide adoption, so optimal test campaigns move to S2 2027 and the engineering-adoption edge becomes soft. The advocate treated autonomous stands as a High input.
debates.resolution: Narrowed optimal test campaigns to development tests and kept S2 2028 High. 'Typical matrices shrink' is an industry outcome, so engineering adoption stays a hard prerequisite. Stands moved to S2 Medium (S3 High) with 10-25% calendar compression.

debates.topic: Certified UQ margins and SHM detection limits (skeptic vs auditor)
debates.skeptic_view: Both nodes should drop to S2 Medium. Model-form error is still open, data is the gate, and the scorecard default for P6 is Low. Probabilistic criteria have been allowed case by case for years with little uptake.
debates.advocate_view: The auditor, not the advocate, took the other side: re-scope the signposts to method output (not regulator acceptance) and relabel the pathway P1, which keeps High grounded.
debates.resolution: Took the auditor's signpost and pathway re-scopes and kept S2 High for both. Took the skeptic's data gate for UQ margins, the limit of its mass claim to strength-critical members, and its trust-tier wording fixes for 372 and 365. Once the signposts measure capability rather than acceptance, the lack of uptake argues about acceptance, which struct-cert-by-analysis and struct-shm-inspection-credit model.

debates.topic: What paces engine reliability: 230 ground tests or fleet engine starts
debates.skeptic_view: Reliability is still shown one hot fire at a time. About 230 zero-failure trials are needed for 0.99 at 90% confidence unless customers accept model priors. Models cut redesign loops, not demonstration tests.
debates.advocate_view: A Starship flight logs about 65-70 engine starts, so 230 starts accrue in about four flights, and 100 flights a year gives ~3,900 engine-flights. Fleet data plus AI-built hierarchical models set the pace. The hook tells readers the opposite of the S2 base case.
debates.resolution: Both are partly right. The arithmetic and the fleet volume stand. But starts on one vehicle or build lot are correlated, Flights 12-13 had engine-outs and relight failures, and every failure resets a zero-failure count. The hook now says a high-cadence fleet logs 230 starts in a handful of flights, so failure modes, not start counts, pace engines. That is a launch-clock effect, not an AI-math one. The proposed fleet-evidence node was rejected as a near-duplicate of physclock-twin-reflight-clearance plus prop-reuse-extended.

debates.resolution: The node was split as the auditor proposed. Joint budgets on demand have a cognitive gate and stay High in S2. Both S2 and S3 are set to 2028, because the signpost needs publication and P1 lags public access. The open model-form part became a separate data-gated node (Medium in S2, 2030). That addresses the skeptic's band and gate concern without downgrading the solved part.

debates.topic: Thinner flown heat shield: S2 band
debates.skeptic_view: LEO capsules have little radiative heating, so the transferable thinning is smaller. The years follow the sizing shift plus a 12-18 month lag (2030). S3 High is three bands above the P7 default.
debates.advocate_view: S2 and S3 share the chain and the year, so the S2/S3 split has no mechanism; raise S2 to High. Varda's Part 450 licence and in-house shields remove the gates, and there are 2 years of slack.
debates.resolution: The years moved to 2030, and S2 and S3 are both Medium. The no-mechanism point was resolved downward: the node cannot be more likely than its hard prerequisite (probabilistic sizing, now Medium for adoption reasons). The licence and W-6 tiles were added to status as support for Medium.

debates.topic: Cadence economy of 50+ commercial returns a year in S3
debates.skeptic_view: This is a market and licensing outcome with no AI-math lever. Moving from about 3 returns in 2026 to 50+ is a >10x increase, and slip ratios run 1.5-3x or worse. Low in every scenario.
debates.advocate_view: Varda names automation and labour as its binding constraint, and S3 brings AI-run operations and factories. Licensing is already compressing. S3 should be High.
debates.resolution: Low in every scenario (>2031/2031/2030). Demand, landing sites and rideshare slots bind ahead of labour. The auditor's exclusion of Starship returns removes the route by which launch cadence alone would satisfy the node. Licensing and heavy cadence are linked as soft edges.

debates.topic: SBLI turbulence closures
debates.skeptic_view: Closures are trained and validated on DNS and ground data, not flight. Out-of-distribution generalization is where ML RANS closures fail, and +/-15-20% approaches the experimental scatter. S2 should be Low.
debates.advocate_view: DNS is compute-bound and compute grows about 3.4x a year. In S3, cap-physics-theory is High from 2028. Change the gate to cognitive and raise S3 to High.
debates.resolution: S2 dropped to Low and S3 kept at Medium, with the data gate kept. More DNS does not fix out-of-distribution failure, and blind validation still needs ground experiments. Both lenses agreed to make the pipeline edge soft.

debates.topic: AI-run aerothermal design loop

debates.advocate_view: The capability branch rates engineering adoption High in S2 2028 and AI-native spacecraft High in S2 2029. The threshold is only a design review citing AI-surrogate trades, so raise S2 to High.

HBM thermal closure is still open. A derivative payload flies 12-18 months after design-complete, and SpaceX schedules run 1.5-3x long.

debates.topic: Where the AI-math lever sits and how to price it (radiators vs solar vs chip temperature; tonnes vs $/GW)
debates.skeptic_view: Radiator design optimization is not a binding mass lever. Solar is 56% of AI1's mass, and every kg/m2 off the array is worth ~6x the same cut on the radiator. Allowable chip/HBM temperature is a bigger lever than design. AI math is worth a few percent of launched mass. Proposed a T5 hot-HBM qualification node gated by qualification.
debates.advocate_view: Tonnes undercount the value once launch is cheap. Thermal is the largest $/GW sensitivity in Mach33's model (+/-30% -> +/-8.9%). The T^4 chip-temperature lever is unlocked by AI wear-out models, proposed as a T3 node at High by 2028. Also proposed an orbital-ground cost-parity outcome node.
debates.resolution: Both currencies now appear in the text: ~2-9% of launched mass, and ~3-7% of $/GW, about 0.3-0.6 year on Mach33's cost curve. Hot chips are a single merged T5 node (qualification gate, Medium in every scenario) with AI applied math as a soft P1/P5 accelerator. Physics-of-failure models already exist at chip vendors, and validation needs life tests plus flight telemetry, so High by 2028 overstated the AI share. The cost-parity node is rejected: it rests on one commercial forecaster, its year depends on which terrestrial benchmark is chosen, and contract prices are rarely disclosed.

Every node except the debris-removal anchor has a hard prerequisite chain back to tier 0.
